market_question: Will the Republicans win the 2028 US Presidential Election?
reasoning: Historical win rates and fundamentals suggest the Republican candidate should have close to a 50% chance. Market-implied 38.5% is too low, even considering uncertainties about incumbency and candidate fields. The party has won roughly half of recent elections, and a large discount is unjustified.
evidence_points: Republicans have won 6 of the last 11 presidential elections since 1980, indicating a natural win-rate near 50%.
Whether or not the party is incumbent in 2028, historical incumbency advantages typically add 2-5%, not a 12-point deficit.
The market’s price likely overreacts to short-term narratives; long-run fair value should regress toward 50%.
